itens.titulo: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
itens.resumo: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

itens.titulo: Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover
itens.resumo: A critical flaw in MongoDB Server allows an unauthenticated attacker to send two requests that trigger a crash on the database server. The crash occurs only if that server is later chosen to take over as the main server while it still lacks some recent changes. itens.titulo: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
itens.resumo: A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2, can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday. itens.titulo: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
itens.resumo: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose. The Threat Research team at Material Security spotted the campaign and has since taken down hundreds of attacker domains in an effort the team calls Operation CloudFire.
